Just found a bloody corpse near the abandoned farm on Cordon.\nLooks like a bloodsucker's work.
Oh, these tushkanos! I've had it!\nThe rookie camp is crawling with them again,\nso if you're scared of rodents, stay away for now.
A pseudodog was seen under the bridge not far from the camp on Cordon.\nAnyone heading that way, be careful.
Cats turned up from somewhere at the checkpoint by the Garbage crossing.\nThey tear around like mad and you can barely get through.\nAnyone who can, please help clear them out.
A bloodsucker tore up a group of bandits at the vehicle graveyard on the Garbage.\nEveryone be careful.
A herd of flesh was seen near the catacomb entrance at Agroprom.
A fire poltergeist cooked a group of stalkers at the Agroprom factory.
Something like a bloodsucker was just seen out in the open at Agroprom.
A pseudogiant was spotted by the rusty bus at Agroprom,\nsitting there resting, the bastard. Probably came from far off.
Picked up the soldiers talking at Agroprom.\nThey were calling for backup: a big pack of dogs jumped their base.
Just now, not far from the swamp in Dark Valley,\na pack of pseudodogs took down two boars.\nNot a sight for the squeamish.
At the Army Warehouses farm, pseudodogs dragged off a stalker.\nIt's about to turn into a bloodbath.
A pseudogiant sat down for a rest by the old bus stop at the Army Warehouses.
Last night I saw two or three more bloodsuckers move into the bloodsucker village.\nCreepy!
A big herd of flesh ran through the Freedom minefield.\nHalf of them died, and the rest are still hanging around out there.
Snorks spotted in the swamp at the Army Warehouses.\nNobody told me how many. Don't get caught.
Attention all! This is the Duty outpost on the Garbage.\nWe have a controller in plain sight by the construction site. We need help.
All hunters, a controller has appeared by the railway bridge in the Gut.\nA strong one, they say. Be ready for surprises.
A couple of hours ago a chimera hit us on the hill by our camp.\nMauled the boys. Be careful out there.
I was heading from Dark Valley to the Gut and ran into an electro chimera.\nBarely got away.. How did it get there?..
A poltergeist showed up at the burned farm in the Marsh..\nHomesick, maybe..
Marsh. An electro chimera was spotted north of the machinery yard.\nGuys, watch yourselves out there..
Scientists in the western Marsh picked up stray psy radiation.\nJudging by the frequencies, they think a controller has turned up.\nSome help wouldn't hurt...
Yesterday we recorded a sturdy bloodsucker in the Marsh near the railway.\nWhere is Duty looking..
Guys, anyone going to Sidorovich, stay clear of the Lost Village -\na burer has made itself at home there.
Borzyi's thugs are in a jam: a burer moved into the tunnel next to them\nand howls all night.\nThey don't know what to do..
A controller came out of Limansk into the Red Forest..\nAlmost put a lot of people down on the bridge.
Electro tushkanos ran into Limansk from Tesla and stirred things up..
A controller's got himself settled behind the building in Limansk...\nLet's hope he don't wander into town..
Dead City. We are observing several electro chimeras.\nWe need help.. Anyone nearby, please respond.
Something's up with the Tesla zone, there are more electro chimeras...\nWonder what that means.

Caught a call from some stalkers asking for help...
they were shouting that they ran into a chimera. $where.
By the time I found them they were dead. And you know...
it wasn't a chimera that killed them, I swear...
they're covered in burns, like from an Electra... anyway, be careful.
Some new filth has probably moved in here.

Stalkers! A few hours ago Duty took heavy losses from unknown creatures.
Anyone with information on mutations in the Zone's creatures
since the last Blowout, please help.
The attack happened $where.
Sapsan, observing a firefight $where...\na group of stalkers is fighting a large mutant... can't make it out... descending.\nAnd switch channels, this one is being monitored...

Duty reports some new kind of chimera. A raid of theirs fell apart...\nThey were going to clear a mutant lair, $where, and suddenly... well, the squad was torn apart in seconds.\nAnd that was no ordinary chimera... it can't... that many men at once...

The ecologists say something's off with chimeras since the Blowout...
some strange new mutations... careful.
And if it helps anyone, I saw a chimera a while back. Running around, the beast, $where.
God knows if it's a normal one...
Stalkers! According to our data, an... unusual creature has appeared $where.\nMost likely a new kind of chimera, mutated by the last Blowout.\nBe careful.

...you think that in the end this may cause entirely unnecessary casualties?
Oh, come now!
Stalkers die constantly from all sorts of manifestations of the Zone, and the lucky survivors
prefer not to ask how their... colleagues die.
So what? I doubt the appearance of one more creature will provoke any serious reaction from the stalkers.
They have seen worse $where.
I confirm the report of the creature.\nSend a squad with heavy weapons.\nThere, $where, my men can do nothing.

Damn... all right, listen up.
Today $where I ran into a military patrol. It doesn't look good, to put it mildly...
you can hardly call it a patrol. All that's missing is guts hung in the trees. I only knew them by the uniforms...
So here's the thing. First, they may send a punitive raid here, or worse, a chopper.
Second, and that worries me far more, some new creature has settled here.
Nothing I know of can rip up a patrol that fast.

Right now $where I'm watching an electro chimera.
It just put down a group of stalkers with quite a firework.
So if you feel like wandering around here, think twice.
Turning back beats lying here with a smoking ass like these poor bastards.
Thinking aloud
%s should hear about this
%s will appreciate the work
%s is waiting for news
%s will be pleased with this
The thing is dead, and %s has waited long enough for good news...
Looks like that's dealt with. %s will surely appreciate it
Done - %s will be glad
All targets down - %s will appreciate that
Bandits dug in $where, five or so. If you're headed there, go around.
Someone is shaking people down $where. They let me go because I had nothing to take. You might not be so lucky.
Borov's men are sitting $where, guns out. Go around if you want to live.
Boars bedded down $where and trampled the place overnight. They may leave by day. Or not.
Blind dogs took over the old lair overnight, $where. You can hear them from far off.
Boars are back in their old nest $where. Plenty of meat, if they don't start first.
Sure, sure.
How do you know?
Bull.
A guy told me the same thing. Then he disappeared.
Don't jinx it.
Get off the channel, you'll drain the battery.
I believe it. Saw something like it myself.
So what, ask to go back to the mainland?
If anyone finds my tent in the morning - there's vodka in it, hands off. I'll be back.
Detector's beeping and I see nothing. Guess I'll go around. That's how we live.
At the fire last night they said the Zone remembers everyone. I don't know what it remembers about me, but I'd rather it didn't.
Anyone seen Boar? Not the animal, our guy. He owes me two hundred rubles and a can of stew.
They say artefacts roll right under your feet after a Blowout. For some reason only anomalies roll under mine.
Quiet today. I don't like it when it's quiet.
Anyone got bandages to trade? Or at least advice on doing without.
Heard shooting, then silence. Then shooting again. Somebody's stubborn.
Someone was screaming on the Garbage half the night, then stopped. Nobody went to look in the morning.
They say the soldiers at Agroprom are jumpy. What they're guarding, nobody really knows.
The rookies on Cordon are arguing again about who reaches the Garbage first. It'll settle itself, as usual.
Sidorovich raised his prices again. Or did I get poorer? Can't tell.
Beyond the Barrier people lose their minds, they say. Who says? The ones who never went.
Anyone know why the dogs are howling tonight? Me neither. I'm staying by the fire.
There was this guy, always meant to go north. They found his backpack by the embankment. Just the backpack.
Bolts run out faster than luck. An old stalker told me that. Never saw him again.
The soldiers at Agroprom are in a foul mood. Some papers went missing, they say. You didn't hear it from me.
Barkeep's perked up, asking people about Dark Valley. Wonder why.
Someone went down under Agroprom and came back. Won't talk about it, just drinks.
The bandits in Dark Valley have got really bold. These days you either pay or you don't go.
Army patrols in the south are rarer now, but meaner. Or maybe it's just me.
I heard someone paid big money for some documents. Too bad not to me.
Snipers are at it in the Wild Territory. Don't know whose. Keep your head down.
They killed a mutant near Agroprom and now there are two in its place. The Zone hates an empty spot.
The lab in Dark Valley went quiet again. Someone went in there and came back, can you imagine?
They say the scientists at Yantar are up to something. Asking for people, paying well. Suspiciously well.
My head hurts more and more whenever I get near Yantar. Not just mine.
More and more zombies around Yantar. Better not to think where they come from. Thinking is bad for you there anyway.
Freedom is partying at the Warehouses and Duty is counting rounds. They'll be at it again soon.
Someone is seriously heading for the Radar. Packed up, said goodbye. We poured him a vodka for the road.
Heard about X-16? Me too, only heard. The ones who saw it have nothing left to tell it with.
They're taking bets at the Bar on whether anyone reaches the center this year. So far nobody's betting yes.
Something changed at Yantar. My headache's gone, and the zombies wander around like everyone forgot about them.
They say Sakharov isn't himself - the instruments at Yantar are showing something odd. Glad or scared, you can't tell.
You can leave Yantar alive now. I don't know who to thank. Probably better not to.
People are whispering about the Radar more and more. Something could be done there too, they say, if you get that far.
At the Warehouses they say someone shoots from the Radar side at night. Who is the question.
The Red Forest has gone quieter. I don't like that.
Limansk isn't quite empty, they say. Someone trades there, can you imagine? In Limansk!
Someone went to the Red Forest for artefacts. Came back without a backpack, and very fast.
They say the Scorcher went quiet. Some people already left to check. None of them are back yet.
The Radar is quiet. First time I can remember. It's scarier than when it was running.
Freedom and the loners are drifting to the Radar. Whoever gets there first is right.
Now everyone will rush north. For loot, for glory, for their own bullet.
The Monolith guys have gone wild. Someone must have taken something from them.
The old hands say Pripyat is open now. Old hands say a lot of things, while they're alive.
Prices on Radar artefacts will drop, you'll see. Or rise. I wouldn't know, I've never been.
Whoever shut it off is either a hero or a dead man. In the Zone there's usually not much difference.
Barkeep poured me one for free yesterday. Don't get excited - then he called in a favor, and I wish I'd paid.
A new guy at the Arena again. My money says we won't see him twice.
Duty's searching everyone at the checkpoint again. Keep a straight face and walk through.
It's calm on Duty ground. Calm and dull - that's why you can't squeeze into the Bar.
Anyone who's been to the Sanatorium, tell me honestly, is it always that quiet? Or only when I'm alone?
The beds at the Sanatorium are all made. I won't ask who makes them.
The road to the Sanatorium is bad. I don't mean potholes.
I was at the Sanatorium. Took nothing. Don't advise you to either.

"Mayday"!

Signal source: $level.

$name.
$name. $level. Can't walk, can't stop the bleeding. Anyone close, answer me.
Wounded. $level. No medkit. This is $name, in case it matters.
Anyone hearing this, $level, I'm the only one left. Leg's smashed. $name.
$level. I'm hit, I won't get far. Somebody come. $name.
Guys, this is $name. $level. I'm down, can't get up. I'll pay what I've got.
Need help, $level. Don't leave me. $name.
$name here. $level. Bad wound, lots of blood. Battery's dying.
If anyone's passing - $level. I'm lying by the road, alive for now. $name.
$level. $name here. Got shot. Don't know who, didn't see. Come get me, will you?
That bloodsucker by the farm, your work? My men at the post can finally sleep at night. This is for you, and we never met.
You cleared all the tushkanos out of the camp? Well, thanks. Now the rookies can stop climbing on crates. Here.
You took down the bloodsucker at the vehicle graveyard? Respect. Duty remembers that kind of thing. Here.
They say the flesh by the Agroprom catacombs are gone. Not big game, but people can walk there easier now. Here.
The fire poltergeist at the factory, that was you? The boys it burned used to drink here on credit. This is on the house.
So that thing at Agroprom really was a bloodsucker? Was is the word. Here, for your trouble.
You put down the pseudogiant by the bus? Well, well. For that you get more than a drink from me.
Three pseudodogs at the farm? That guy won't come back, but others can get through now. Thanks. Here.
So the giant by the bus stop is gone. I don't need extra corpses at the Warehouses. Here, you won't be short-changed.
You settled three bloodsuckers in that village? Didn't think anyone would go in. Here, take this.
You cleared the flesh off our minefield? The boys were already betting on which one blew up next. Here.
Snorks in the swamp are finished? I never did find out how many there were. Well, now you know. Here.
The controller by the construction site is dead? The outpost owes you, and Duty pays its debts. Take this.
The controller by the bridge is down? Then the hunters can go back there. Good hunting, stalker. Here.
The chimera from the hill is your trophy? Thanks for the boys. This is from the whole camp.
You killed that electro chimera that almost got me? Then I owe you. Here.
The electro chimera by the machinery yard is gone. Duty doesn't forget that. Take this.
Three controllers?! The scientists thought one, and maybe imagined at that. You're a beast. Here, you earned it.
The bloodsucker by the railway is no longer being recorded. It's nice when an observation ends this way. Here, please take this.
You killed the burer in the Lost Village? We were already planning the detour. Thanks, friend. Here.
The burer in the tunnel has shut up. My boys finally sleep, and I finally get to wake them. Here, you earned it.
The controller from the bridge, done? Respect. My lot would only have wasted ammo. Here, you earned it.
So you're the one who cleaned up that controller? Thanks, son. At least he won't wander into town now. Here.
Both electro chimeras in Dead City are dead, our instruments confirm it. Please accept this with thanks from the whole group.
One electro chimera less in the Tesla zone. That answers the question for now. Here.
Forget what I asked - someone already killed that thing. Who, I don't know.
No need to hurry: they say that thing is already dead, no thanks to us.
Matter closed. Some people dealt with that thing. Job's done.
Anyone going after that thing can stay home. You're too late.
That beast isn't a problem anymore. Someone quicker turned up.
Forget what I asked - $name killed that thing. Lucky for him.
Anyone know a guy called $name? He's the one who put that thing down. No need to go.
Matter closed: $name dropped that thing. He's the one I'm pouring for now.
Bandits are shaking down everyone $where. Rookies had better stay away.
Bandits blocked the way $where. Pay or go around.
The bandits have more men now, $where. They barely let me pass.
While everyone rushes north, the bandits have got bold $where. Go around.
Borov's men are lying in ambush $where. I saw them first. You might not be so lucky.
Borov is gone, but his boys aren't, $where. Angry now, and with no boss.
Some bandits have dug in $where. How they even got this far, I don't know.
Mercs are waiting for somebody $where. I wouldn't check who, if I were you.
Mercs are holding the road $where. They shoot without warning.
The bandits are getting brave $where. They wait for anyone coming back with loot.
Even here there are bandits now, $where. Set up so you can't walk past.
Flesh wandered in overnight, $where. You can hear the grunting from far off.
They cleared out the boars, and they're back $where. New ones, just as mean.
Blind dogs took the lair back, $where. They howled so much the post couldn't sleep.
Pseudodogs have settled $where. More tracks after one night than in a train station.
Snorks came out $where. It was empty, and they took it overnight.
A bloodsucker is back in the old den $where. Didn't see it, but the tracks are fresh.
A whole herd of flesh is standing $where. Hunters will be pleased.
A pack took over the ruins $where. Better not go there at night.
Tushkanos are breeding $where. Small, but they'll have your leg off.
A bloodsucker has moved in $where. The Red Forest was no resort as it is.
Snorks are back $where. The scientists asked me to pass on: keep away.
A pack of pseudodogs $where. Big ones, never saw them like that here before.
Snorks crawled out once the Scorcher stopped, $where. Nature hates a vacuum.
Bulldozer
A boar has turned up $where. The guys call it Bulldozer: it has trampled two already. I won't let rookies go. Anyone tougher, help out.
You killed Bulldozer? At least the rookies can walk there now. Thanks. Here.
Stub
A boar with a broken tusk is about, $where. The guys call it Stub: it has crippled two of mine already. Duty will pay for it.
Stub is done? Respect. My men will rest easier. Take this.
Quiet One
They say a bloodsucker is dragging people off $where. My customers call it Quiet One. Whoever brings word that it's gone won't regret it.
So Quiet One is gone. My customers will be glad, and I keep my word. Here.
Limper
A pseudodog called Limper is hunting $where. It has cost me three customers already. I'll pay whoever stops it.
Limper is gone? Good for business. Here, you won't be short-changed.
Neighbor
A bloodsucker has moved in $where. My boys call it Neighbor, because someone vanishes every night. Whoever removes it won't be sorry.
So Neighbor moved out? My boys can sleep now. Here, you earned it.
Torn Mask
A snork called Torn Mask is following people $where. Careful out there, it has tracked men down more than once.

Shot $mob $where. My hands are still shaking, but it's over.
Ran into $mob $where and killed the lot. I'm fine, hardly any ammo gone.
Shot $mob $where. That's something, for me.
Shot $mob $where. I think I did it right.
Shot $mob $where. Small fry, but not a scratch on me, and that's good enough.
Put down $mob $where. A small pack, and I'm in one piece.
Went one on one with $mob $where. Put it down without a scratch.
Finished off $mob $where. Spent more on ammo than it was worth.
Shot $mob $where while passing. Not worth mentioning.
Easy work: put down $mob $where. Didn't even break a sweat.
Small fry. Put down $mob $where, the round cost more.
Tushkanos are tushkanos. Put down $mob $where, no loot worth the name.
Put down $mob $where, the whole bunch. A minute's work.
Put down $mob $where in one go. It happens.
Had to work for it against $mob $where, but no losses. Dead for sure.
Put down $mob $where. Used more ammo than I expected.
Ran into $mob $where and killed the lot. I'm fine, only my hands shake.
Dealt with $mob $where, though I froze at first. Dead for sure, nothing lost.
Put down $mob $where, but I had to reload twice. They're all down.
One on one with $mob $where took a while, but I put it down. Don't ask how.
Finished off $mob $where. Was a bit scary, but I managed and I'm in one piece.
Dealt with $mob $where. Familiar business.
Put down $mob $where without fuss. Spent a fair amount of ammo.
A small scuffle with $mob $where. Dead for sure, no wounded.
Dealt with $mob $where. They came in a crowd, but they're all down now.
Shot down $mob $where. Just the one animal, but with character.
Put down $mob $where. Knew where to hit, so no losses.
Barely put down $mob $where. Thought I wasn't getting out.
Put down $mob $where, and I barely made it out myself. Never going back there.
Almost stayed $where for good, went up against $mob. But it's dead for sure, and I'm still shaking.
Got hit $where, but I put down $mob. Out of bandages now.
First time I saw such a beast up close. Put down $mob $where, don't know how, and I'm alive.
I'd only heard of those before. Put down $mob $where, my legs are still like cotton.
Put down $mob $where. Ran, shot, ran again. They're all down, I'm alive, thank God.
The fight with $mob $where was heavy. Put it down, but I'm out of bandages.
It was a hard fight with $mob $where. Dead for sure, but I took a hit.
Put down $mob $where. Don't joke about it: hard, costly, and you always run out of ammo.
Got hit $where, but I still put down $mob. Need some patching up now.
Put down $mob $where, every one. The pack was vicious, took one in the side for it.
Hit the legs and never stood still, that's how I put down $mob $where. Going there, take more ammo and keep your distance.
One on one with $mob $where was harder than I expected. The beast is down, I'm barely on my feet.
Finished off $mob $where, but it cost me. Next time I take a partner.
Put down $mob $where. Hands are shaking, but it's nothing serious.
Ran into $mob $where. Handled it. I think.
There's my first mark: shot $mob $where. The old-timers say it's small fry, but I'm pleased.
My first tushkano $where, yeah. I'll skin it, might get a couple of rounds' worth.
Shot $mob $where. Small fry, but I didn't miss, kind of proud.
Took down $mob $where and didn't get hurt. Almost can't believe it.
Put down $mob $where, there were a few. Didn't run, can you believe it? Surprised myself.
Stopped by on business and shot $mob $where on the way. Not worth mentioning.
Put down $mob $where on the way. Spent a round, the trip goes on.
Dropped $mob $where in passing. No loot in it.
Shot down $mob $where. Small stuff, as long as it doesn't get in the way.
Tushkanos are tushkanos. Put down $mob $where and moved on.
Put down $mob $where, the whole bunch. A minute's work, then moved on.
Dropped $mob $where with one shot. Nothing special.
Put down $mob $where, took some work. Keep your head down and learn, an old hand told me. I'm learning.
Got through $mob $where, though I froze at first. Pack's intact, and that's what matters.
Shot $mob $where, I just got tired of reloading. But I'm fine, yeah.
Ran into $mob $where, dead for sure. Barely any ammo left, will have to tighten up.
Put down $mob $where, every one. Shot and prayed, to be honest.
Just the one animal, but it chased me through the bushes. Still, I put down $mob $where and I'm in one piece.
First time I saw what kind of beast it is up close, and I put down $mob $where. Legs like cotton, but alive.
Put down $mob $where. They ran around trying to scare me while I just shot. Funny now.
Put down $mob $where, but got roughed up a bit. It'll heal.
Dealt with $mob $where. Sorry about the ammo, otherwise a regular trip.
Finished with $mob $where. Don't go there without spare ammo, that's all the advice I have.
Had to work against $mob $where, but no losses. Dead for sure.
Put down $mob $where. A small pack, I fired from cover, they came straight on.
Put down $mob $where. Just the one, but stubborn. Hit it from a distance.
Put down $mob $where. Hit the legs and don't stand still, then no losses.
Put down $mob $where. Small stuff, but it shows its teeth if you wait. Didn't wait.
Ran into $mob $where. Ran, shot, ran again. Dead for sure, alive, thank God.
Almost stayed $where for good, but I put down $mob. A week of rest now.
Got hit $where. Bandaged up, finished off $mob and now I'm sitting here shaking.
First time I saw such a beast up close. Put down $mob $where, and my hands are still shaking.
The old-timers told me, and I didn't believe it. Now I do. Put down $mob $where, barely survived.
Put down $mob $where, but there were too many. Barely breathing, damn, thought I wouldn't make it.
Just the one beast, and I nearly gave up the ghost. Put down $mob $where, legs like cotton.
Put down $mob $where, but I nearly stayed there for good. Going there, don't go alone.
An old wolf, and still nearly paid for meeting $mob $where. Dead for sure, but hit the legs and don't stand still.
Put down $mob $where. Hit hard, but the lesson stands: don't go there alone.
Hit the legs and don't stand still. Only that way did I put down $mob $where, nothing else worked.
Put down $mob $where. A pack, and a nasty one. A box of ammo, two bandages, but they're all down.
Put down $mob $where. Just the one, but it cost ammo like ten. Got hit, but alive.
Finished off $mob $where, but it cost me. Next time I take a partner.
Took a few shots at $mob $where just to stretch. Boring, boys.
Put down $mob $where. Not a fuss, just a warm-up.
Whacked $mob $where quietly. The boss wouldn't even notice.
Dropped $mob $where for lack of anything better. Piece still warm, and zero cut.
Squashing tushkanos is no job, just play. Whacked $mob $where, that's it, boys.
The small stuff $where got on my nerves, listen. Put down $mob and went on with the job.
Put down $mob $where, boys. A couple of rounds each and nobody squeaked.
Just the one, listen. Put down $mob $where with a single round, for real.
Ran down $mob $where. Spent a few rounds, but we got ours, for real.
Tangled with $mob $where. Picked up some scratches, but it's dead. Our guys are alive.
Dropped $mob $where, small expense. The gun works like a clock, bro.
Whacked $mob $where. Burned a pile of rounds, but no losses.

Squad broken. Reinforce patrols, account for losses.
Defeat. We draw conclusions and don't forget the fallen.
The men are dead. Duty doesn't forget its own.
Eh, they lost. Pour one, we'll remember the boys.
Sad, but free folk keep their heads up. To them!
They lost, but they lived free. Let's drink.
Squad destroyed. Losses confirmed, noted.
Defeat recorded. Reinforcement required.
Personnel lost. Reporting to HQ.
What a tragedy. We are very sorry.
They lost. We are sorry for all who died.
More losses. We ask everyone to be careful.
Sometimes it goes without shooting.
Fine. Back alive, that's good enough.
So the trip was for nothing. But safe.
A bust, I see. Main thing nobody got hurt.
The trail went cold, it happens. Don't be upset.
Better without a fight. Get some rest.
A dud, it happens. At least the ammo's intact.
At least nobody lost. Go warm up.
Called off is called off. Not every trip brings loot.
A dud, damn. Wasted legs, boys.
Meh, no profit and no action. Boring.
Slipped away quietly, lost nobody. Fine.
No luck, but no stiffs. It happens.
Understood. Stand down, personnel rest.
No losses, no fight. Order is kept.
Task cancelled, men intact. Keep reporting.
No fight? Then pour one and to the campfire!
Ha, found nothing, fought nothing, no big deal.
Stand down is stand down. The guitar's waiting.
Stand-down received. Enemy not detected.
Noted. No contact, no casualties.
Task not completed, no casualties. Logged.
Sorry nothing was found, but all are safe.
No data, but no losses either. Thank you.
Also a result. Negative data matters.
Good luck to them. Hope everyone makes it back.
We'll see how it ends. I'll keep an eye on the news.
I'll bet a box of ammo it won't go without surprises.
So they're heading out. Hope it's not for nothing.
They're moving out together, good. Hope they get lucky.
Jealous. I'd like a crew like that for my trips.
Don't relax out there, the Zone doesn't like that.
Well, off they go. The Zone will sort out who gets what.
A group is safer. Though in the Zone it's down to luck.
Luck to them. They'll need it.
Yeah, off they go. I'd wait till morning.
The squad has set out. Wishing success and a return at full strength.
Orders given, the men are on the way. Awaiting the report.
Discipline and order. Then it will work out.
Well, boys, break a leg! We'll keep the fire warm for your return.
There go the handsome ones! Just don't forget the guitar.
Bet a bottle they come back with a story?
Copy. Departure logged.
Noted. Awaiting report.
Squad movement received. Good luck.
Interesting. Please tell us if they find anything unusual.
We wish them luck. We will follow the news.
We hope they are careful. The Zone is unpredictable.
Morning. I'd kill for hot tea, but there's no clean water. Who's heading out today?
Dawn. The mutants are still groggy after the night, best time for a run before they wake up.
Barely slept, my legs are like cotton. Oh well, the run won't make itself.
Rise and shine, boys. The sun's up and we haven't made a cent yet.
Morning. Check your guns, somebody borrowed a piece last night and never gave it back, hear me?
Morning, boys. The suckers won't come to the Zone by themselves, we gotta go meet them for a job.
Morning. Guard change. Troops fall in, report overnight incidents to the senior of the post.
Dawn. The night post is handed over, no incidents. Patrol, get ready to move out on the perimeter.
Wake up. Clean your weapons, straighten your uniform. Discipline starts in the morning.
Good morning, free folk! No coffee, but there's tea and a great mood. Pour me a big one.
Dawn, boys. The guitar's still warm and we're already on our feet. Look at us.
Morning, guys. Whoever sang loudest last night lights the fire today. That's the law of freedom.
Morning. Scheduled activities under way. Personnel ready, no incidents overnight.
Dawn. Perimeter checked, shift handed over. Ordered to continue observation.
Morning check complete. No casualties, no remarks.
Morning. Starting measurements, the dawn background readings come first. Please keep quiet near the instruments.
Dawn. Overnight data processed, few samples. We will go into the field as soon as the air warms up.
Morning. Thank you to everyone who stayed away from the camp last night: our observations came out clean.
Evening's coming. Whoever isn't back before dark has only themselves to blame.
Sunset. I'll light a fire and heat up some stew. The Zone is a different place at night.
Evening. Ammo for a run and a half, and I still have to walk back. I don't like it.
Evening, boys. Soon we go out on a job, who's awake and packing?
Evening. The marks with loot are heading to their holes, time to shake them down. No fuss, quiet-like.
Dusk. Whoever's in on it tonight, come over, we'll talk about the cost and the take.
Evening. Reinforce the guards. After dark, leaving the perimeter only by order.
Evening. Patrols, check your comms and weapons. Night shift, take over the post.
Sunset. The lines are closed, keep order. Duty doesn't leave its own behind, nobody goes beyond the perimeter alone.
Evening! We'll light a fire, sing something and forget where we are.
Sunset, boys. Pour me one, the guitar's ready, and the soldiers can shiver in their trenches.
Evening, free folk. Whoever's alive today is a good man. We'll drink to the others.
Evening. Duty handover. Everyone stay on comms.
Sunset. Reinforce posts on the approaches. Report any movement immediately.
Evening. Personnel accounted for, weapons present, no losses today.
Evening. Wrapping up the field work and returning to base before dark. We ask all our people to stay on comms.
Sunset. Compiling the day's data. The background behaves differently in the evening, which is curious.
Evening. Putting instruments into shielded cases. We ask stalkers not to come to us after sunset.
Dead of night. Quiet as a crypt. Anyone awake is either a fool or a watchman.
Night. Something's howling out there. Better not go out.
Can't sleep. Sitting by the fire, listening to the Zone rustle. A bit lonely out here.
Night's our time, boys. Whoever's awake is at work.
At night the suckers hide in the bushes and we go out for a stick-up. Check your pieces.
Night. The boss said sit tight until word comes. Whoever sticks his head out picked his own cell.
Night. The night posts are on duty. Everyone else, rest.
Night. Patrol, report every hour. Allow no strangers to the line.
The night guard is on post. No fire without orders, and sleeping on post is forbidden.
Night, a fire, a guitar. Just keep an eye around us, or we'll get too relaxed.
Night, guys. Whoever's awake gets a song. Everybody else, sleep well, free folk.
Dark as inside a soldier's head, but the stars are nice. Pour me one, boys.
Night. Quiet mode. Night patrols operate as planned.
Night. Sector observation in progress. No movement logged.
Night post taken over. Ordered to open fire on command only.
Night. Elevated background. Do not leave shelter without need.
Night. Observing psi activity, which is more noticeable at night. Please keep quiet.
The night recordings contain odd noises, origin still unclear. We are continuing the work.
Morning. Didn't get enough sleep, but maybe the day will be quiet.
Dawn. Time to pack up while the mutants sleep.
Woke up alive, which is already not bad. We'll see what comes next.
Morning. Anyone going out today, take more ammo.
Dawn, dew on the metal, fingers freezing. At least we got through the night.
The crows are already screaming. So it's morning and we're all still here.
Evening. The shadows are longer, the nerves thinner.
It's getting dark. Better finish your business before nightfall.
The sun is setting. Another day lived, thank God.
Evening in the Zone. Some are heading home, some are heading out hunting.
The sunset's pretty. Shame there's no time to enjoy it while running for cover.
It's getting cold. Anyone who still has to go out, take something warm.
Midnight. The best time for bad thoughts.
Night. Too quiet. That doesn't bode well.
Can't sleep. Listening to the Zone breathe.
Night. Anyone awake, keep your weapon at hand.
Dark as pitch. I'm not switching my flashlight on, you never know who comes to the light.
At night every rustle sounds like a shot. Keep watch in turns, folks.
The first morning after the blowout. Head like a hangover, and the anomalies are not where they used to be.
The morning after the blowout. The survivors are crawling out of their shelters, we're counting our own.
Dawn, and the air still smells of ozone. It was a strong blowout.
You won't recognise the trails after the blowout. Where it was clear yesterday, it may burn today. Throw a bolt ahead of you.
Good morning to everyone who sat out the blowout under a roof. The others, look for them where they were standing.
The mutants are jumpy after the blowout, bolting around the area. Don't wander far.
The sky is washed out, the grass is gray with dust, something got swept into the ravines. No hurry, let it settle first.
Crows have been screaming on the Cordon since morning. Good or bad, I can't tell.
Soldiers smoke at the roadside checkpoint while we freeze in the ravines. I wouldn't walk up to them with a weapon in hand: they shoot first and ask later.
Newbies are heading for the Cordon in a crowd again. First stop is Sidorovich, and they walk out with half their ammo gone and a piece of advice.
Blind dogs run around the rookie village at night. If you're going with just a pistol, think twice.
Walking under the railway embankment on the Cordon is easier than along the top. You can be seen from too far up there.
The Garbage smells of soot and rust, it stings the eyes. I only use trails I know.
On the Garbage it's dog after dog. Blind ones, two or three at a time. Don't spare the ammo or they'll eat you.
The rusty car hulks on the Garbage hide you well, duck in and wait. Just throw a bolt first, in case there's an anomaly.
We bed down in the hangar on the Garbage, at least it has a roof. The echo makes every step sound like somebody else's.
You keep hearing shooting from the Garbage. Either mutants or people at each other, I don't go looking.
The Agroprom research institute grounds are closed to outsiders. Violators will be detained, resisters fired upon.
In the tunnels under Agroprom the water is knee-deep and the dark swallows the flashlight. Don't go down alone.
The soldiers at the institute have been sour lately. They don't like our kind with guns, stay away from the fence.
Dogs keep howling by the institute. Our guard shoots them, but new ones keep coming.
Dark Valley, boys, is our ground. Whoever comes without asking pays up or answers for it.
Hey, suckers are coming into the Valley thinking it's like the Cordon. Explain to them what's what, real clear.
There's a lab under the Valley, X-18. Only psychos go down there for loot and we don't: the howling from underground is something else.
Boars roar in the Valley, no sleep. Dropped one for dinner, at least some profit.
The Bar, Duty territory. Weapons checked at the entrance, one order for everyone.
The post at the Bar entrance handed over, no incidents. Drunks sent back inside, brawlers cooled down.
Fights on the arena again, high stakes. We make sure the brawl after the bell doesn't spill into the street.
It's loud in the Hundred Roentgens bar, but while they drink inside they don't break the peace. Bandits are barred from entry, we turn the extras away.
Whoever comes to the Bar in peace will find a bed and food. Duty doesn't leave its own.
Rostok. The factory shops are under Duty guard. Outsiders enter by command permission only.
The Rostok guard has been changed. The patrol went around the factory perimeter, no remarks.
Something growls in the fog beyond the Rostok shops at times. Orders are not to leave the perimeter alone.
Bandits try to enter Rostok through the wasteland. Our patrol holds the line, nobody has gotten past yet.
It's never dull for Freedom at the Army Warehouses. Plenty of rusty hardware, and the soldiers shoot at shadows half asleep.
Our guys found a whole crate of ammo at the warehouses. Pour me one, guys, or we'll have to share.
Duty looks sideways at our warehouses, and we give them a guitar and a song. Let them be jealous, the pretty boys.
There are plenty of hangars at the warehouses and few free hands. Come to the fire, there's room.
Please do not approach the lake at Yantar without a protective suit: the instruments show what is better left unseen.
Yantar, the bunker. We collect few water samples, and at night we see zombies by the road. We ask that you do not stray far from the bunker.
We are observing the psi background. There are spikes, but we cannot explain them yet.
We ask stalkers not to fire near the equipment at Yantar. The instruments are costly, and we have nothing to repair them with.
Thank you for the artifacts you brought. Please hand them in inside containers and do not touch them with bare hands.
The Marsh is damp and quiet, only mosquitoes whine. You walk and squelch.
The Marsh. Good weather here is like bad weather. Feet wet, cartridges dry.
The reeds on the Marsh rustle even without wind. Don't fire blind, you'll only give yourself away.
Put your foot on a hummock, not on the grass: there's waist-deep water under the grass. Tested, my boots are still drying.
Fog on the Marsh crawls waist-high. You walk blind and hope there's a hummock under your boot.
It's cleared up. So hot the water in my flask is warm as tea. Not even a breeze.
Clear sky, you can see far. Good for a run, but they can see you far too, so keep to the bushes.
The sun's out. Dried my footwraps on a rock, a man can live.
The sun's blazing like a tower floodlight. Boys, stick to the bushes and don't flash, there's plenty of punks with binoculars.
Weather's cleared, for real. Rig the tarp and get in the shade, it's so hot the piece is melting in your hands.
Clear as your palm. Lousy weather for a meet, any sucker spots you from a mile off.
Sky clear, visibility good. Observers, change positions and check your sectors twice.
Heat, soldiers. Drink water on schedule, keep your uniform fastened. Discipline doesn't depend on the weather.
Sunshine, guys! Guitar on your shoulder and out on the grass before the Zone changes its mind.
Clear day, beautiful. The Duty guys are probably stewing in their armor already, and we're in T-shirts.
No cloud cover, visibility maximum. Observation proceeding as normal.
Temperature elevated. Personnel to drink water, helmets stay on in open positions.
No cloud cover, ultraviolet background is high. Please keep your goggles on when handling samples.
Clear, pressure steady. No better time for field measurements, we are heading out to the sites.
The stars are out and it's getting cold. Sitting without a fire: on a clear sky any light shows from a mile off.
The moon shines like a lamp, shadows sharp. Fine for a run, if your nerves are steady.
Clear night, the moon's like a lamp. Lousy for a job, you're in plain sight, so we stay in.
Loads of stars and it's freezing. No fire, no need to flash. Warm up with moonshine, boys.
Night is clear, the moon is full. Sentries, watch closely, silhouettes show on the horizon from afar.
Cold tonight. Issue warm gear to the guard, change shifts on schedule.
Stars, a campfire, a guitar. Pour one, brothers, and let's play something quiet.
A clear night, guys! The Duty boys are nodding off by the book, and we're counting stars.
Night clear, moonlight sufficient. Reinforce the posts, log all movement on the perimeter.
Temperature dropping. Personnel to draw warm clothing.
The sky is clear, conditions for astronomical observation are excellent. A pity the Zone background causes interference.
No clouds, it has turned noticeably colder at night. Please remember warm clothes when going out to the sites.
It's clouded over. No sun, no shadows, and my legs want camp.
The sky is grey and low. While it's dry I should get the loot, it may pour later.
The clouds have settled in, all grey. In murk like this it's right for a quiet job, nobody sees from afar.
The sky's closed over, boys. Nobody sees past fifty steps, so we work, no yawning.
The sky has clouded over, visibility limited. Patrols, report every half hour.
Overcast, rain possible. Check your rain gear, cover your weapons.
Grey, guys, but we're not made of sugar. Who's getting the guitar, who's getting the kettle?
Clouds are here, so what. A grey sky is a great excuse to stay in the sleeping bag.
Solid overcast. Visibility limited, increase observation.
Cloud cover increasing. Precipitation possible, cover the vehicles, move ammunition under the awning.
Cloud cover has increased and pressure is falling. Please seal your samples against moisture and go out without haste.
The sky has clouded over, there isn't enough light for imaging. We are postponing the field shots.
Clouds covered the stars. Pitch dark, you hear everything and see nothing. I don't like this.
A night with no moon. Sitting by the fire, eyes adjust to the dark slowly, so I'm not straying far from the flames.
Dark, not a star. Right time for a job, but in the dark you can't see your own either, don't shoot our boys.
Murk in the sky, dead of night. Search quietly, no noise, clear? Safety on.
Night, overcast, visibility near zero. Sentries, report by voice every fifteen minutes.
No moon tonight, hold the perimeter by ear. Order: do not fire at a rustle without a command.
Dark as a cellar, but we've got a fire and canned stew. Pour one, guys!
Not a star. No matter, we'll sing louder so we don't lose our own in the dark.
Night, solid overcast. Check night vision charge, scan your sector.
Illumination zero. Log perimeter movement by sound.
The sky is covered, stellar observations are cancelled. We will spend the night organizing our notes.
Overcast and damp tonight. We are staying inside, outside only if necessary.
It started drizzling. My cloak has holes, boots squelch, and nowhere to wait it out. The Zone, damn it.
Rain, damn it. Ammo under the cloak, wipe the gun dry, or it'll jam at the worst moment.
Rain, boys. Tracks get washed away, no one hears footsteps, right time to shake somebody down on the road.
Pouring like from a bucket. Clothes soaked, the shack is damp, counting cash beats getting wet.
Rain. Patrols go out in rain capes, cover your weapons. Do not shorten the route.
Rain. Clean weapons after every outing, damp ruins the mechanisms.
Rain, guys! So what, whoever doesn't like it can sit under the awning, and we're going out in it.
It's pouring. I was going to wash anyway, if only I could reach the well.
Precipitation. Visibility reduced, roads washed out. Limit vehicle movement.
Rain has started. Sentries put on rain capes, shield weapons from moisture.
Precipitation has begun. Please do not collect water from puddles: composition not studied.
It is raining, humidity is rising. Cover the instruments, switch off the recorders until dry weather.
Rain at night. The roof leaks in two places, I set out a pot. Sleeping with one eye open.
Downpour and darkness. Stepped out for a minute, came back soaked to the bone. Not going again.
Night downpour, for real. Lookouts, don't doze on watch, in this dark you won't notice anyone sticking you.
It's pouring, no tracks left. You couldn't ask for better weather for a night job, boys.
Rain at night. Guards change more often so nobody catches cold. Do not lower vigilance.
Rain, night. Keep the floodlights off, listen to the perimeter.
Downpour, night, a fire under the awning. Now that's life, brothers. Who said the Zone is hell?
Rain on the roof, a guitar in the warm. Probably the best night this week.
Night precipitation. Motion sensors give false alarms, cross-check with visual observation.
Rain, visibility zero. Sentries rotate hourly, check weapons after each shift.
Rain at night. The lab windows are sealed, equipment under plastic. We are continuing work.
The noise of rain interferes with audio measurements. We are working with documentation, not going outside.
A thunderstorm is coming. Artifacts in the container, and I stay away from metal and tall trees.
Thunder's started. Find cover before it hits close, and don't stand under a lone tree.
Thunder and lightning. Even the punks hide in their holes, time we got indoors too. We sit, we don't twitch.
It cracked so hard my teeth hurt. Boys, get in cover, stay off the hills, lightning finds you in the open.
Thunderstorm. Leaving the perimeter is forbidden, pull the sentries off the towers for the duration.
The storm is starting. Ground the antennas, check radio contact every ten minutes.
A thunderstorm, brothers! We'll sing louder than the thunder. Just don't sit under a tin roof.
Thunder's here! Who's coming to the porch with me to watch the lightning?
Storm front. Ground the antennas, shut off electrical equipment, personnel to shelter.
Thunderstorm. Suspend vehicle and foot movement until it ends.
A thunderstorm has begun, electrical activity has risen. The instruments show noise, we are halting measurements.
Please disconnect sensitive equipment from the mains and avoid open ground during the storm.
A thunderstorm at night. Flashes across half the sky, no sleep, I jump at every crack.
Thunder rolling, and something howls even louder out there. Door propped shut, gun within reach.
Night thunderstorm, boys. Don't go out on a job, one bolt and you won't even get to write a note.
Thunder hits like a drum, the dishes rattle in the shack. We sit, whoever sticks his head out is his own enemy.
Thunderstorm at night. Reinforce the posts, wired contact only, no light signals.
Night storm. Guard stays in shelter, patrol only inside the perimeter.
A night storm, beautiful! The fire hisses, the thunder shakes your chest. Pour one, guys.
What a racket! Bet even the Duty guys won't sleep tonight.
Thunderstorm at night. Communications noisy, transmit only what's needed, repeat codes twice.
Flashes disrupt night vision gear. Observation by naked eye only.
A night thunderstorm, readings jump. The lab is on backup power, we are recording data by hand.
The storm is overhead. Please do not leave instruments switched on, lightning damages electronics.
Clear and hot. The water in my flask runs out faster than the loot in my pack.
The sky is clear. You can see far, and you can be seen from far.
A good day. I almost forgot where we are.
Sun and not a cloud. A rarity around here.
Clear. Dry and warm, the time to dry your wet things.
Not a cloud since morning. Dust everywhere, better tie something over your face.
Plenty of stars. So quiet you can hear your own heart.
A clear night. You could read by the moon, if only there was a reason.
Cold and clear. Something howls far away, but I pretend not to hear.
The night sky is clear. A rare time when it's actually beautiful.
The moon is bright, shadows like in daytime. You walk, and they can see you from a mile.
Clear and chilly. The fire hugs the ground, the wood's damp and the night is cold.
The sky is overcast. No sun, no shadows, just grey.
Overcast and damp. My joints ache, so it'll rain.
The clouds are low and heavy. Better not relax today.
Grey sky, grey faces. The kind of day you don't feel like talking.
Clouds are hanging low. Got my cloak out just in case, can't hurt.
No stars, no moon. The night is like a black sack over your head.
Dark and damp. The fire barely holds, and it hisses.
Clouds cover the sky. You can't see a thing, and you hear too much.
An overcast night. High time to sit in cover and not stick your head out.
So dark I can't see my own hand. If I trip, it wasn't me, it was the Zone.
Rain comes in sheets. Every track is washed away, for better and for worse.
Wet and chilly. You wade through puddles and wonder what it's all for.
The rain won't let up. If only it would stop for an hour.
Under a downpour even the mutants hide. At least that's some use.
Rain started. Water runs down my collar and the shelter is still a long walk.
It pours at night. The drumming on the roof is like a metronome, no sleep.
Rain and darkness. Better not go out, though the water is coming in anyway.
A night downpour. Everything alive has gone under a roof.
It drips and roars, footsteps are inaudible. A bad night.
Rain at night, wood's wet, the fire won't catch. Going to bed cold and soaked.
The thunder cracked so loud horses would have crouched. If there were any here.
A thunderstorm overhead. Stay away from metal and tall trees.
Lightning strikes nearby. Not the best time for a walk.
The sky is black as tar and the lightning cuts it to pieces.
The storm began, my hair stands on end, and not from fear. Time to find a roof.
A night thunderstorm. The flashes are so bright every stone shows.
Thunder, lightning, downpour. A good night to regret going out.
A flash, then the crash. I count the seconds between them, it doesn't help.
A thunderstorm in the night. Even the dogs have fallen silent.
Lightning hit really close. Now my ears ring and I've got white spots in my eyes.
Dawn's come, and without clouds. The day looks promising.
Dawn, dew, silence. If you don't think about where you are, almost a resort.
The sun rises clear. It'll be a hot day, fill your flasks this morning.
A clear, chilly morning. While it's fresh, the time to go for loot.
The sunset is red as blood. But tomorrow should be clear, they say.
A quiet evening, a clear sky. It's rare.
The sun is setting, it's getting cold. Time to find a place for the night and gather wood.
A clear evening, the distant ridges like a painting. If only every day were like this.
A grey, overcast dawn. Don't expect the sun today.
A grey morning, you can't see beyond a hundred paces. To go or to wait, that is the question.
A dull, sluggish dawn. Zero energy.
Damp and cold this morning, barely got the fire going. Some hot coffee would be nice.
Evening that feels like night already. The clouds ate the sunset.
Dusk falls fast. Heading to camp while the road is still visible.
It's getting dark early because of the clouds. Better get back before night.
A grey evening, a cold wind. The night will be like a cellar.
A wet dawn. My clothes haven't dried since yesterday.
Morning, and outside it's the same. Rain.
Dawn in the rain. Grey, damp, kettle on the fire and sit tight.
It poured toward morning. The trails turned to mud, feet sink.
Evening, pouring. Sit in the warm and listen to the drops.
Rain since evening. Tomorrow the roads will be mud.
Evening falls and the rain won't stop. It'll be fully dark soon, need to get under a roof.
The rain got heavier toward evening. The cloak doesn't help anymore, soaked through.
The morning starts with thunder. A good sign? No.
A storm at dawn. Better wait it out.
Dawn, yet the sky is black and there's lightning. Some morning.
Thunder at first light. Put out the fire, loot under cover, waiting.
An evening storm. Flashes over the horizon, beautiful and scary.
A storm toward night. Shut the shutters.
It started thundering toward evening. Better not stay out in the open.
Evening, and the thunder is getting closer. Run for camp.
The blowout's over. Come out, those who are alive, and count the losses.
We survived the blowout. The sky is clear and the mood is foul. They say new artifacts have appeared.
The blowout is over. Whoever got to cover is still in business. Sympathies to the rest.
It's over. Boys, anyone alive? Count heads, check the gear, then we'll see about the cut.
Blowout ended. Check the posts, count the personnel.
Blowout over. Report losses, give aid to the wounded, restore the perimeter.
The blowout's gone! We're alive, so we'll live on. Hey, who's up for artifacts?
It's passed, brothers! Climb out of the cellar, the fire won't light itself.
Blowout ended. Report losses. Personnel to leave the shelters.
Blowout complete, losses being recorded. Man the posts within ten minutes.
Blowout completed. Recording background changes and expecting a new wave of anomalies. Please do not go for samples right away.
The blowout has ended, instruments record a background spike. Please wait for readings to stabilize before going out.
The blowout is done. The sky is clear, only ringing in the ears.
That's it, you can go out. Those who are alive, answer.
That's over. Now artifacts, looters and silence.
Survived. Every time feels like the last.
My hands are still shaking. A smoke, a gulp of water, then loot.
The sky turned red and went back to normal. Better not recall how it looked.
